headline: "The most serious crisis since Iraq's invasion of the country in 1990": Blockade of the Strait of Hormuz paralyzes Kuwait, whose oil provides more than 90% of public revenues
summary: Kuwait remains paralysed six months into the Middle East conflict, unable to transport oil on which it depends for over 90% of public revenues. Iran has also regularly targeted the emirate with strikes.
why: Kuwait is a major OPEC crude producer, and its oil export revenue funds most of the state budget, so export disruption hits both its fiscal position and global crude supply.
